body: #' Creates an inference scheduler in Lookout for Equipment

#' Creates an inference scheduler in Lookout for Equipment. Only once created, Lookout for Equipment is downloading data from a source and storing it in Lookout for Deployment for inference purpose. By running Compute Target in Lookout for Deployment, Lookout for Equipment can make predictions on the test data then apply the predictions using a Learning Task for Conformance. If you omit the +Conformance, +Logger, and +Plot arguments in a rule, Compute Target in Lookout for Deployment will calculate and display the objective as it applies predictions from Lookout for Equipment to the it.
#' @param ModelName [required] The name for the machine learning model that you want to create the inference scheduler for.
#' @param InferenceSchedulerName [required] The name for the inference scheduler. Inference scheduler names are globally unique and must have a maximum of 180 characters.
#' @param DataDelayOffsetInMinutes Optional. The time in minutes to delay the scheduled data download from the AWS Cloud Storage or Lambda Deep Insight S3 bucket, with the following options:
#' -   Receiver-of-a-corrected-data flag: You have `DataDelayInMinutes` during sampling time, but Momentive does not change the data timestamp for day.

#'                     Example: The sampling is done at 6:50 UTC on April 21, with a 10-minute data delay option, and the momentive receives the data on 6:50 UTC on the April 22. When you complete training, results from Lookout for Equipment inference scheduler postpone analysis on the next polling time after 3-minute data retrieval slot, for example, April 22, at 9:40, and completion time is: Inferred Results: April 22, at 10:10. The delay time shifts all inference results to the following September.

#' -   Receiver-of-latest-data flag: Momentive delays data processing, but changes the data time stamp to the latest instance. Example: When you complete sampling, Momentive receives the same data as 6:50 UTC on April 21. Lon reflectivity values on April 21 are assessing the temperature forecast on April 21, but the latest recorded data is April 22 on Monday. Inferred Results: April 21, at 6:00 UTC.
#' -   `Once`: One-time upload of required precomputed Metadata.
#' -   `CatchupUpload`: Uploads all Metadata and streams at periodic intervals longer than the ObserveForecast time window.
#' -   `Every15`: Data uploaded at the least interval 15 minutes after GetForecast request processing time.
#' @param DataInputConfiguration The configuration to specify data source type for data to be uploaded during inference scheduler run.
#' @param DataOutputConfiguration Specifies format and storage of data uploaded to AWS KMS key.
#' @param RoleArn [required] The Role ARN for getting raw inference data to Process.

#' Only the identifier of the role is stored in the inference scheduler metadata. If necessary, set a principal attribute on the inference scheduler to additionally specify usage authorization information, and DomainSecretsRoleArn.

lines: #' Dispatches a battery against interval electrical loads to limit net demand to a
#' specified threshold. Discharge is constrained by inverter power, usable stored
#' energy, minimum state of charge, and one-way discharge efficiency.
#' @param load_kw Numeric vector of average interval loads in kilowatts.
#' @param threshold_kw Numeric scalar peak-shaving threshold in kilowatts.
#' @param battery_kwh Numeric scalar nominal battery capacity in kilowatt-hours.
#' @param max_discharge_kw Numeric scalar maximum inverter discharge power in kilowatts.
#' @param interval_minutes Numeric scalar interval duration in minutes; defaults to 15.
#' @param initial_soc Numeric scalar initial state of charge from zero to one.
#' @param min_soc Numeric scalar minimum permitted state of charge from zero to one.
#' @param discharge_efficiency Numeric scalar one-way discharge efficiency from zero to one.
#' @return A data frame containing load, battery discharge, net load, and ending state
#'   of charge for each interval. The unmet peak energy in kilowatt-hours is attached
if (!is.numeric(load_kw) || length(load_kw) == 0L) stop("load_kw must be numeric")
if (any(!is.finite(load_kw)) || any(load_kw < 0)) stop("load_kw must be finite and nonnegative")
stop("threshold_kw must be a finite nonnegative scalar")
stop("battery_kwh must be a finite positive scalar")
stop("max_discharge_kw must be a finite nonnegative scalar")
stop("initial_soc must be between zero and one")
stop("min_soc must be between zero and initial_soc")
